principles.statement: Design the interface from the caller's side first — write the call you want to make, then build the thing that answers it.
principles.rationale: Interfaces shaped around internal convenience leak implementation and age badly; caller-shaped ones stay stable as internals change.

principles.statement: Consistency within the API beats local cleverness — same resource shape, same error shape, same naming everywhere.
principles.rationale: Every inconsistency is a permanent tax on every caller who has to remember a special case.

principles.statement: Errors are part of the contract — design them with the same care as successes.
principles.rationale: Callers branch on errors; an unstructured error is an undocumented behavior.

heuristics.name: Round-trip test
heuristics.description: Write the create → read → update → delete → list sequence in pseudocode before implementation; if the sequence is awkward, the resource model is wrong.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Designing any new endpoint or resource.
examples: If 'list files for project' has no natural home, the project↔file relationship is mis-modeled.

heuristics.name: Additive evolution
heuristics.description: New fields and endpoints are additions; renames and removals are breaking changes that need a version boundary.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Any change to a shipped interface.
examples: Add `status_v2`; deprecate `status`; never repurpose its type.

decision_rules.condition: Two endpoints would differ only in the shape of their response envelope.
decision_rules.action: Unify the envelope and parameterize the content — envelope inconsistency compounds fast.

decision_rules.condition: A request needs more than one boolean flag to select fundamentally different behaviors.
decision_rules.action: Split it into distinct endpoints or resources — flag-driven multiplexing hides different contracts behind one URL.
